text:
maya: quick sync — planning a small holdback bakeoff for the new model bring-up (gpt-3.5-xl variant). goal: agree on quant sweep flavors + manifest fields before we publish to the optimize registry. want deterministic fallback semantics and gating thresholds.

raj: yes — we should include AWQ, GPTQ, INT8 (dynamic), and FP8 where supported. run same eval-suite v2 (lm-eval-lite, qa-subset, rouge-agg).

olivia: preliminary numbers from yesterday's run:
- fp8: median perplexity +0.8%, p95 +1.6%
- awq (w8a): median +1.2%, p95 +2.4%
- gptq (4-bit): median +2.9%, p95 +6.3%
- int8-dyn: median +0.6%, p95 +1.1%
So FP8/int8 look promising; GPTQ has larger tail regressions on qa-subset.

liam: we need a manifest schema that encodes: flavor id, quant_engine, quant_bits, expected_delta_{median,p95}, eval_snapshot_hash, consumer_hints (latency/cost buckets), and fallback_chain. propose minimal fields in registry entries so runtime can pick safe fallback.

chen: +1. Also add a field `holdback_tag` for canary gating (e.g., "hb-10pct-7d"). gating logic: fail rollout if p95_delta > 3% OR median_delta > 1.5% on any core eval.

maya: here's a tiny example manifest snippet we can standardize on (feel free to nit):
```
flavor: "xl-awq-w8a-1"
quant_engine: "awq"
quant_bits: "8"
eval_snapshot: "sha256:3a7f..."
expected_delta_median: "+1.2%"
expected_delta_p95: "+2.4%"
consumer_hints: ["latency:<100ms","cost:low"]
fallback_chain: ["fp8-compat-1","int8-dyn-1","hosted-full-fp32"]
holdback_tag: "hb-10pct-7d"
```

raj: small ask — use string-encoded numbers for deltas and canonicalized hint keys (latency_ms, cost_class) so SDK parsing is trivial. also include `model_family` and `pin_version` for traceability.

olivia: noted. re-evaluated gptq with higher calibration steps — p95 improved to +4.5% (still above our gate). will attach the run hashes to the PR.

liam: runtime behavior: when a request arrives, server should consult routing policy -> if flavor not available or delta exceeded at runtime (observability signal), it should follow `fallback_chain` sequentially. add a TTL for cache entries so rollbacks propagate quickly.

chen: for Redwood Optimize recs, we should surface two profiles: `optimize:cost` and `optimize:latency` with recommended `consumer_hints`. e.g., cost profile suggests `batching:aggressive, kv_cache:true, quant_engine:awq` while latency profile suggests `batching:single, kv_cache:true, quant_engine:fp8` (if fp8 meets gate).

optimize-bot: auto-check: holdback runs queued on infra pool `bakeoff-2` (job 6548). baseline eval-suite v2 assigned. ETA ~3 hours.

maya: action items:
- olivia: push gptq calibration run hashes + attach eval CSV to PR (due EOD)
- liam: draft manifest schema PR with canonical keys + sample parser (due tomorrow)
- raj: add gating rules to rollout docs, include `p95` and `median` thresholds
- chen: wire Optimize UI to show holdback_tag and recommend profile (follow liam's keys)

olivia: will do the CSV and add a short note about observed failure modes (QA hallucination spike on gptq).

raj: if all good, we can canary `hb-10pct-7d` next week. :thumbsup:

maya: thanks — keep updates in this thread and @maya when PRs are ready.
